fields.h1: Build a Cookie Order Form That Fits Your Baking Schedule
fields.hero_description: Get a cookie order form that prices each order by the dozen and saves it to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What the Form Handles Before Pickup
fields.features_subheading: A cookie order form asks every customer for the same details. These six parts end the copying of orders off texts.
fields.feature_1:
Built from a description of your menu

Emergent builds the form from a plain-English list of what you sell, such as three flavors sold in dozen boxes. Ask for a seasonal flavor later, and Emergent adds it.
fields.feature_2:
One question per screen on a phone

Customers answer one question at a time, which suits an order placed from a link in a social post. Ask for the pickup date early, since it decides what you can still offer.
fields.feature_3:
Each order saved as a row you own

Every order lands in a database you own, with the pickup date beside the customer's phone number. Next November, look up last year's buyers and send each of them the new menu.
fields.feature_4:
A live count of dozens per pickup day

A dashboard updates as orders come in and adds up the dozens booked for each pickup day. By Tuesday you can see if Saturday will need a second batch of sugar cookie dough.
fields.feature_5:
Order totals sent to your books

The form connects to any tool with an API, such as QuickBooks. Each order total then reaches your books without retyping, and the full order stays in your own database.
fields.feature_6:
No response cap in December

Emergent puts no cap on responses. A holiday rush never closes the form for hitting a plan limit, and the only limits are the ones you set, such as boxes per pickup day.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Cookie Bakers Take Orders
fields.tab_content_1:
No rush order is confirmed until the baker accepts it

Wildrose Cookie Co. needs 7 days to make a decorated custom set. Delia Marchetti asked for 3 dozen baby shower cookies with pickup in 5 days. The form marked her order pending and sent owner Tess Halloran a Slack direct message to accept or decline. Noor Abbasi, with 12 days' notice, was confirmed at once.
fields.tab_content_2:
Once December 23 has 80 boxes, it closes

Thornapple Bake House bakes 80 Christmas cookie boxes for each pickup day. When the 80th box for December 23 was booked, the form stopped offering that date. The next customer saw December 22 instead, which had 52 of 80 boxes booked and 28 still open.
fields.tab_content_3:
From 4 dozen up, each dozen costs $32

Fairhaven Cookie Studio sells logo cookies at $36 a dozen, or $32 a dozen from 4 dozen up. Pellston Dental ordered 6 dozen with its tooth logo for a patient open house. Office manager Lena Quist saw the $192 total on the form before she sent the order. Had she picked 3 dozen, the form would have shown $108.
fields.tab_content_4:
Pickup windows reach every Saturday customer on Friday

Copper Kettle Cookies hands out orders from its front counter in 30-minute windows. This week, 14 orders were booked for Saturday pickup. At 10 am Friday, each of the 14 customers got an email with their window. Ines Pardo's email said 11:00 to 11:30 am for her 2 dozen snickerdoodles.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Cookie Order Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a cookie order form that books only what you can bake and tells each customer when to pick up.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Set a limit for each day
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Price it the way you quote it
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Ask for the date before the design
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide how many days' notice each kind of order needs, such as 3 days for a plain dozen and 7 for a decorated set. Anything with less notice becomes a rush order that waits for your answer.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Count what your oven and your evenings can turn out in one day, in dozens or in boxes. Take the number from your busiest week last year, not your best day, and use that as the daily cap.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write the prices the way you give them on the phone: per dozen, with any break for larger orders and a flat fee for custom designs. The form shows the customer the total before they send the order.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Put the pickup date and quantity ahead of any design questions. A customer then learns a day is full before writing out a theme. Keep one notes field at the end for colors, wording on the cookies, and allergies.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste the rules you wrote above into one prompt. Emergent builds the form with its order database and alerts. Change any part later by asking, such as adding a pumpkin flavor in October or raising the daily cap.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Choose when the reminder goes out
fields.howto_step_6_des: Pick a time the day before pickup for the reminder email. Put the pickup window and your address in it. Nobody then has to text you to ask where to go or when to come.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Place one ordinary order, one rush order, and one for a day that is already full. Check that each one lands in the database and that the rush order reaches you. Delete the test rows afterward.

faq_plan.q: What is needed in a cookie order form?
faq_plan.ref: what is needed in a cookie order form
faq_plan.a: A cookie order form needs the customer's name and phone number, the pickup date, the flavors, and the number of dozens. For custom work, add design notes and an allergy question. Ask for the date first, which lets the form hide pickup days that are booked up.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a cookie order form?
faq_plan.a: Describe it in plain English to Emergent's AI form builder: what you sell, your price per dozen, your lead time, and how many orders you can bake in a day. Emergent builds the form and the database behind it. Ask for changes the same way, such as adding a holiday box.

faq_plan.q: Is there a cookie order form template I can start from?
faq_plan.a: Yes: a written description of your menu works as the template, and the form is built to match it. Name your flavors, box sizes, and pickup days, and Emergent builds a cookie order form template around them. The orders it collects stay in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: What should a Christmas cookie order form include?
faq_plan.a: A Christmas cookie order form should list each box or tin with its price, the December pickup days you offer, and a cap on boxes per day. Close ordering a few days before your last pickup, which gives you one shopping trip for butter and flour. If your holiday sale also sells shirts, keep those on a separate t shirt order form.

faq_plan.q: What should a cookie dough order form include?
faq_plan.a: A cookie dough order form should list each flavor with its tub size and price, the number of tubs, and a delivery or pickup date. If the dough is frozen, ask when the buyer can collect it. For a group sale, add a field for the seller's name, and every tub is credited to the right person.

faq_plan.q: Can I get a cookie order form template free?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent is free to start, and the free tier covers building and publishing a cookie order form. Describe your menu and pickup rules, then share the form as a link. A short menu and one pickup rule are enough for a first version.

faq_plan.q: How does a custom cookie order form handle design requests?
faq_plan.a: It asks for the design as part of the order: the occasion and colors, plus any wording. Treat each custom set like a work order form, with one record per job and a status you change as the set moves along. A look at the pending sets tells you what to bake this week.

faq_plan.q: How should I price orders on a custom cookie order form template?
faq_plan.a: Start with a price per dozen, then add what changes the work: a lower rate for large orders, a fee for extra colors, and a rush fee if you take short-notice sets. Write each rule down before you build the template. Emergent builds the form so the total updates as the customer picks a quantity.

faq_plan.q: What should a decorated cookie order form include?
faq_plan.a: A decorated cookie order form should ask for the occasion, the colors, any lettering, the number of designs in the set, and how the cookies are packed, such as individually bagged. Set a limit on designs per dozen, for example 3, before a customer asks for 12 different cookies. Ask about allergies in the same form, not in a follow-up text.

faq_plan.q: Why use a digital cookie order form instead of paper?
faq_plan.a: A digital order form saves each order with its pickup date in one place, not on slips by the register. Customers can also order at night, when nobody is there to answer the phone. Keep a paper pad at the counter for walk-ins, and type those orders into the same form.

plan.angle: The top 10 for cookie order form is printable templates and template galleries: a blank sheet with name, phone, flavor and quantity lines. None of them shows what a cookie baker actually fights: rush requests, a holiday pickup day that overbooks, price breaks by the dozen, and customers who forget pickup. This page shows a cookie order form that handles each one for four bakers a searcher will recognize, and the FAQ covers what the form needs, holiday, custom, decorated, cookie dough and digital order forms, plus free templates.
